skills.trigger: When evaluating a retrocardiac cystic or consolidative lesion in the lower lobe on chest CT to distinguish pulmonary sequestration from other cystic lung diseases.
steps: Identify the location and morphology of the lesion, specifically looking for a retrocardiac mass with air-fluid levels or cystic changes in the lower lobes.
Assess the adjacent lung parenchyma for signs of hyperinflation or compensatory emphysema, which suggests a chronic congenital anomaly rather than an acute process.
Systematically trace vessels in the mediastinum and diaphragm region on contrast-enhanced images to identify an anomalous systemic arterial feeding vessel arising from the aorta.

Differentiate from lung abscess (which lacks a systemic feeder and typically presents with acute infectious symptoms) and bronchiectasis (which shows bronchial dilation without a distinct systemic supply).
